title: Mermaid Diagram Authoring Scrolling Review
summary: Short Mermaid syntax, selection, debugging, and readability briefs for reviewing diagram authoring one screen at a time.
audience: Developers and technical writers learning to read, create, and maintain Mermaid diagrams.

cards.title: Declaration Comes First
cards.prompt: The first meaningful line selects the Mermaid grammar for every statement that follows.
cards.explanation: Use declarations such as flowchart, sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, stateDiagram-v2, or erDiagram before writing relationships.

cards.title: IDs Are Not Labels
cards.prompt: Keep source IDs short and stable while visible labels explain the domain idea.
cards.explanation: In Gateway[API gateway], edges reuse Gateway. The human-facing API gateway label can evolve without changing every relationship.

cards.title: Direction Guides Layout
cards.prompt: LR, TD, TB, RL, and BT request a reading direction rather than fixed coordinates.
cards.explanation: Mermaid's layout engine positions nodes. Authors describe relationships and a preferred direction instead of placing pixels manually.

cards.title: Label Decision Outcomes
cards.prompt: A decision reads faster when every outgoing edge names its outcome.
cards.explanation: The diamond asks one question while Yes and No live on the relationships that represent the possible answers.

cards.title: Group Real Boundaries
cards.prompt: Use subgraphs for ownership, trust, deployment, or domain boundaries—not decoration.
cards.explanation: A named boundary should help the reader reason about responsibility or communication across it.

cards.title: Sequence Means Time
cards.prompt: Read sequence participants across the top and messages from top to bottom.
cards.explanation: Sequence diagrams answer who communicates at each point in a scenario; they are not static dependency maps.

cards.title: Sequence Control Blocks
cards.prompt: Choose alt for alternatives, loop for repetition, and par for concurrent work.
cards.explanation: Each block communicates a different runtime rule; using the precise block reduces prose and ambiguity.
cards.code:
alt Approved
  API-->>Web: 201
else Rejected
  API-->>Web: 409
end

cards.title: Class Diagrams Are Static
cards.prompt: Class diagrams show types, members, inheritance, composition, and dependencies.
cards.explanation: They explain structure independent of one request. Use a sequence diagram when message order is the real question.

cards.title: State Means Legal Next
cards.prompt: A state diagram makes lifecycle transitions and forbidden paths reviewable.
cards.explanation: Durable conditions belong in states; temporary calls and responses belong in actions or sequence messages.

cards.title: Read Crow's Foot
cards.prompt: Exactly one customer may own zero or more orders in this relationship.
cards.explanation: The customer-side double bar means exactly one; the order-side circle and crow's foot mean zero or many.

cards.title: Schedules Become Stale
cards.prompt: A Gantt diagram is a maintained documentation snapshot, not a project-management backend.
cards.explanation: Assign ownership and review dates, durations, and dependencies whenever the underlying plan changes.

cards.title: Journey Scores Need Context
cards.prompt: A journey score is an author judgment unless its measurement source is named.
cards.explanation: Use the 1-to-5 scale consistently and avoid presenting illustrative sentiment as product analytics.

cards.title: Pie Needs A Whole
cards.prompt: Use pie charts for a few categories that form one meaningful total.
cards.explanation: Time series, negative values, and many similar slices need an axis-based chart or table instead.

cards.title: Mindmaps Use Indentation
cards.prompt: Whitespace defines hierarchy in a Mermaid mindmap.
cards.explanation: Consistent indentation is semantic. Use a flowchart instead when branches need explicit arrows or decisions.

cards.title: Timeline Is Not Gantt
cards.prompt: Use timeline for chronology; use Gantt when durations and dependencies matter.
cards.explanation: Both involve time, but only the Gantt grammar models scheduled work and dependency-driven starts.

cards.title: Reduce Before Repairing
cards.prompt: How would you isolate one syntax error inside a large Mermaid block?
cards.explanation: Keep the declaration and one valid statement, then restore lines until the first failing addition identifies the parser boundary.

cards.title: One Question Per Diagram
cards.prompt: What is the fastest way to improve an everything-architecture diagram?
cards.explanation: Split it into focused views with explicit questions and consistent abstraction levels instead of adding more color or smaller text.

cards.title: Test The Host Version
cards.prompt: A diagram working in a current editor may fail in an application with an older Mermaid dependency.
cards.explanation: Version-sensitive and experimental grammars must be tested with the same package version, configuration, and security mode as production.
